t: Section 2304c(e) of title 10, United States Code, is amended by striking paragraph (3).

fable.w: The section is a bare technical amendment that strikes a paragraph of 10 U.S.C. 2304c(e); its text sets up no comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation with outside parties, or right to sue. The tempting reading is that section 2304c(e) concerns protests of task and delivery orders, so removing a paragraph (likely a sunset) might indirectly preserve a protest right. But the section itself does not grant or describe any outside-party process, so on its text it does not recommend or require participation.

opus.w: This section only makes a technical amendment striking a paragraph. On its face, it does not create a comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation with outside parties, or a right to sue or object. Reading it as participation would depend on outside knowledge that the struck paragraph was a sunset on task-order protest rights, and nothing in the given text shows an outside party taking part in a federal decision.
opus.s: Section 2304c(e) of title 10, United States Code, is amended by striking paragraph (3).
opus.b:
1. **Tempting reading:** 10 U.S.C. § 2304c(e) deals with bid protests of task and delivery orders, and paragraph (3) was, as I recall it, a sunset clause on the protest right. Striking a sunset would keep in force a way for outside contractors to formally object to a federal contracting decision. That would count as participation.

   **Why it fails:** That reading depends entirely on outside knowledge of what paragraph (3) said, and I can't confirm that from the text given. The section itself only strikes a paragraph. It doesn't grant anyone a right to protest or sue, set up a hearing or comment period, or require consulting anyone outside the federal government. Judged on its own text, it describes no outside-party process. If paragraph (3) really was the protest sunset, the answer could be "Yes," which is why my confidence is only moderate.

qwen_chat.w: This section is a legislative amendment instruction that removes a specific paragraph from an existing statute. It does not establish, require, or describe any process of consultation, coordination, or participation with parties outside the federal government. The text itself contains no actors or processes related to public participation.
qwen_chat.s: Section 2304c(e) of title 10, United States Code, is amended by striking paragraph (3).
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might think that deleting a paragraph could remove a participation requirement, or that the context of the deleted paragraph (which is not provided here) might imply participation. However, the text itself is purely a legislative amendment instruction ("is amended by striking paragraph (3)"). It does not describe any process of consultation, coordination, or involvement with outside parties. It is a procedural change to the statute's text.
